name: Until Death Do Us Part
summary: In Silverpine Forest, Until Death Do Us Part brings Clarice Foster’s old grief to Yuriv’s grave. From the Pools of Vision beneath Thunder Bluff, the Forsaken asks you to leave her keepsake pendant on the tomb of the husband who abandoned her and their children.

sections.title: A Bitter Keepsake
sections.body: Clarice Foster remembers her mortal marriage without fondness. As Lordaeron crumbled, Yuriv left her and their children to join a crusade against the rising undead, declaring service to the Holy Light paramount. His devotion saved neither his family nor himself. Clarice was raised into undeath, while Yuriv lies beneath a defaced stone. She wants the last tangible reminder of his broken promises cast away.

sections.title: The Neglected Grave
sections.body: Yuriv’s tomb lies in the graveyard around the Sepulcher, marked by gashes, rubbish, and weeds. Set Clarice’s pendant on the relief of his sculpted hands, and no grand magic or spiritual closure follows. The gem grows dull, and a cold, silent gust passes over the tombs, leaving the old resentments of Lordaeron’s fallen people.

faq.answer: Yuriv was Clarice Foster’s mortal husband. He left her and their children to fight the Scourge in the name of the Holy Light, putting his crusade before his family.

faq.q: Why does Clarice hate her late husband so much?
faq.answer: Clarice waited night after night while Yuriv put his religious duties first. His crusade failed to protect them; he died in a neglected grave, and she was raised as the undead kind he fought.

faq.q: What happens when you return the pendant?
aliases: ending of until death do us part
faq.answer: On the stone hands carved into Yuriv’s tomb, the pendant’s gem grows noticeably dull. A stiff, cool breeze sweeps over the Sepulcher, where the defaced grave lies in silence.
Yuriv’s tomb is in the cemetery at the Sepulcher, a Forsaken stronghold in northern Silverpine Forest.

faq.q: Why is Yuriv's grave so damaged?
faq.answer: The grave is gashed, littered with garbage, and overgrown with weeds. The Forsaken at the Sepulcher feel no sympathy or reverence for a crusader who died fighting their kind.
Clarice says Yuriv abandoned his children along with her, but gives no word of their fate. With Lordaeron devastated, they may have met a tragic end.

angles.text: As Forsaken, you can see Clarice’s plight as the hypocrisy of the living: holy warriors left their families to perish in holy fervor, while their transformed survivors bear the burden of memory.
As a priest, you can see how devotion to the Light can tear families apart and leave lasting bitterness in those left behind.
As Horde, you gain a glimpse of the personal tragedies and enduring spite that bind the Forsaken in Silverpine Forest.
